- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–25% to compensate for bearish bias.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >15% from prior day), model often overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 20–40% for the next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently underestimates in the 10–15 day horizon; apply a 15–25% upward bias for medium-term (10–30d) forecasts.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model shows mean-reversion bias; adjust forecast toward recent 7-day average, not long-term trend.
- Model overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; for 30d forecasts, smooth sentiment impact over 5–7 days to avoid erratic corrections.
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >20% in 3 consecutive days, apply “reversion penalty”: reduce next forecast by 15–25% to avoid runaway momentum.
